title: Lipschitz stability for multilinear random polynomials
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $F,G$ be real coefficient families indexed by subsets of $[n]$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be independent random variables. Suppose each $X_i\in L^4(\mu)$, $\int X_i\,d\mu=0$, and $\int X_i^2\,d\mu=1$. For every $c\ge0$ and every $c$-Lipschitz $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
\[
\left|\int\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i\right)d\mu-\int\psi\left(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}G(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i\right)d\mu\right|\le c\,\|P_{F-G}\|_2,
\]
where $P_{F-G}(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}(F(S)-G(S))\chi_S(x)$ and the norm is taken under the uniform measure on the Boolean cube.
hypotheses_covered: Coefficient families $F,G$ indexed by subsets of $[n]$
A function $\psi$ that is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$
